title: Phase Kickback
summary: A controlled gate acting on an eigenstate of its target changes the control, not the target.
objectives: Prepare the target qubit in |−⟩, an eigenstate of X
Predict which qubit of a CNOT changes when the target is an eigenstate
Identify the eigenvalue of the target as a relative phase of the control
mission: Prepare the control (qubit 0) in |+⟩ and the target (qubit 1) in |−⟩, then apply a CNOT from qubit 0 to qubit 1. The target keeps its state; observe the control.

prediction.question: The target is in |−⟩, an eigenstate of X with eigenvalue −1. The control is in |+⟩ and you apply a CNOT. Which qubit changes state?
prediction.explanation: The target stays in |−⟩. The sign −1 from X appears only in the term where the control is |1⟩, so it is a relative phase of the control, which goes from |+⟩ to |−⟩.

hints: The target must be in |−⟩: apply X to take it to |1⟩, then a Hadamard.
The control in |+⟩ needs a Hadamard on qubit 0. Apply the CNOT last.

challenge.mission: Kick back a phase of i. Prepare the control (qubit 0) in |+⟩ and the target (qubit 1) in |1⟩, an eigenstate of the S gate with eigenvalue i. Then apply a controlled phase gate (cp) from qubit 0 to qubit 1 that acts as a controlled-S. The target stays in |1⟩ and the control must end in (|0⟩ + i|1⟩)/√2. Only x, y, z, h, cx, cz and cp are allowed, so the phase i has to come from the cp angle.
hints: A controlled-S multiplies the |1⟩|1⟩ component by i. The S gate is the phase gate with angle π/2.
Prepare the target with X, the control with a Hadamard, then use qc.cp(angle, 0, 1) with angle = π/2.
qc.x(1), qc.h(0), qc.cp(pi / 2, 0, 1), with `from math import pi`.
